_comment: Bible designer, axis 1 of 5 (story/designer/INTERVIEW.md). Questions are a guide: ask them in your own words, one per turn, and skip any the project or an earlier answer already settles, saying why. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY.
goal: Know what the book is, whether it is invented or from the record, what already exists, and what the author has already had to look back for.

questions.ask: In a sentence or two, what is this book about?
questions.why: It names who or what the book follows and where, which decides which later questions are worth asking.
questions.listenFor: the main person or group, the setting, what drives the story or the history forward

questions.ask: Is it invented, or drawn from the record — real people and real events?
questions.why: In nonfiction every value needs a source; the designer seeds nothing the author or the sources have not stated.
questions.listenFor: invented / real / a true scaffold with invented people; where the sources are

questions.ask: Is anything written yet — chapters, an outline, notes, a spreadsheet? I'll read it before I ask you anything it already answers.
questions.why: Reading first means confirming instead of asking cold. An author asked to retype their own outline stops answering.
questions.listenFor: chapter count, an outline, an existing tracker and what is in it

questions.ask: What have you already lost track of, or had to go back and look up?
questions.why: This is the real need. The tables exist to answer these lookups; a column no one would look up is clutter.
questions.listenFor: a number that drifted, who had an item, when someone learned something, a rule broken by accident

doneWhen: You can say in one line what the book is, whether it is from the record, and the two or three lookups the tables must answer.
